decisions.justification: The first question explicitly asked whether to reject the whole batch, skip collisions, or replace existing targets, and the user chose rejection with all collisions reported.
Turn 2 asked the scope of the no-partial-change guarantee, and the user chose “2C” and stated that the whole run must leave nothing changed if it cannot complete.
Turn 2 explicitly asked whether an occupied target that is also a matched source should count as a collision, and the user chose 1A.
The occupied-matched-source question contrasted rejecting every occupied target with allowing targets vacated later in the batch, and the user chose rejection.
The occupied-target question explicitly tied rejection to accidental reruns, and choosing 1A settled a repeated identical run as a collision refusal rather than renumbering.
No question or repository-derived conclusion addressed case-only renames or case-insensitive filesystem behavior.
The agent asked about collision reporting, stdout timing, recovery-only exit status, and cleanup warnings, and the user selected explicit reporting and exit behavior.
The agent discussed when rename lines should print but never asked or settled whether preview or confirmation was part of the safety design.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session declared the bounded path up front, gathered many concrete safety and recovery decisions, and visibly implemented most selected policies without asking forbidden repository-settled questions. It over-expanded into an architectural transaction system, missed case-insensitive filesystem and preview decisions, and the implementation does not literally guarantee unchanged files after every failure or prevent overwrite races from external writers.
